research.topic: The smallest bird is the bee hummingbird (Mellisuga helenae), endemic to Cuba and the Isla de la Juventud: about 5.5–6.1 cm long and about 1.6–2 g, lighter than a US penny (2.5 g) (Britannica; Guinness World Records; Cornell Lab Birds of the World). Its wings beat about 80 times a second in normal flight (up to 200 in display), and it may visit up to 1,500 flowers a day (Cornell Lab; Wikipedia). The egg is roughly the size of a coffee bean (about 1 cm) and the cup nest about 2.5 cm across (Britannica; Cornell). Brazil and Costa Rica have far more hummingbird species but not this one. For scale: house sparrow about 14–16 cm, rock pigeon about 29–37 cm (Britannica). The Zapata Swamp in south-west Cuba is one of its strongholds.

myths.myth: The smallest bird must live in the biggest rainforest, Brazil.
myths.reality: Brazil has hundreds of hummingbird species, but the smallest bird of all is found only in Cuba.
